answer.method: Freedman approximation for log-rank test power. if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")
  library(powerSurvEpi)
}

# Study parameters
n_per_group <- 200
hazard_ratio <- 0.7
event_prob_treatment <- 0.3707
event_prob_control <- 0.4890
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate power using powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default
# The function uses the Freedman approximation for log-rank test power
# Parameters: 
#   k = number of groups (2 for treatment vs control)
#   n = total sample size
#   p0 = event probability in control group
#   p1 = event probability in treatment group
#   lambda0 = baseline hazard (can be arbitrary, we set to 1)
#   lambda1 = treatment hazard = lambda0 * HR
#   sided = 2 for two-sided test
#   alpha = significance level

# Total sample size
n_total <- 2 * n_per_group

# Using powerCT.default from powerSurvEpi
# The function signature: powerCT.default(k, n, p0, p1, lambda0, lambda1, alpha, sided)
# where p0 and p1 are event probabilities in control and treatment respectively

# Set arbitrary baseline hazard
lambda0 <- 1
lambda1 <- lambda0 * hazard_ratio

power_result <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  k = 2,                          # 2 groups (treatment and control)
  n = n_total,                    # total sample size
  p0 = event_prob_control,        # event probability in control
  p1 = event_prob_treatment,      # event probability in treatment
  lambda0 = lambda0,              # baseline hazard
  lambda1 = lambda1,              # treatment hazard
  alpha = alpha,                  # significance level
  sided = 2                       # two-sided test
)

# and verify the critical value usage is correct

library(powerSurvEpi)

# Parameters
nE <- 200
nC <- 200
pE <- 0.3707
pC <- 0.4890
RR <- 0.7
alpha <- 0.05

# Call the function directly to confirm
result_from_package <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  nE = nE,
  nC = nC,
  pE = pE,
  pC = pC,
  RR = RR,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("Function Result from powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default\n")
cat("================================================\n")
cat("Power:", result_from_package, "\n\n")

# Manual calculation to verify the two-sided structure
# The formula used: power = Phi(sqrt(k*m)*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1) - z_{1-alpha/2})
# The z_{1-alpha/2} is for two-sided with alpha/2 in each tail

k <- nE / nC
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC
z_two_sided <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # For two-sided test

# This is the non-centrality parameter for the log-rank test
nc_param <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(RR - 1) / (k * RR + 1)
test_stat <- nc_param - z_two_sided

# Power is the probability of rejecting under the alternative
power_manual <- pnorm(test_stat)

cat("Detailed Formula Check (Two-Sided Test):\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("For two-sided test at alpha = 0.05:\n")
cat("  Critical value z_{1-alpha/2} = z_{0.975} =", z_two_sided, "\n")
cat("  (This is the two-sided critical value)\n\n")

cat("Non-centrality Parameter:\n")
cat("  NC = sqrt(k*m) * |RR-1| / (k*RR+1) =", nc_param, "\n\n")

cat("Test Statistic for Power:\n")
cat("  Z = NC - z_{critical} =", nc_param, "-", z_two_sided, "=", test_stat, "\n\n")

cat("Power Calculation:\n")
cat("  Power = Phi(Z) =", power_manual, "\n\n")

# Verify this matches
cat("Verification:\n")
cat("  Package result:", result_from_package, "\n")
cat("  Manual calculation:", power_manual, "\n")
cat("  Difference:", abs(result_from_package - power_manual), "\n")
cat("  Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(result_from_package, power_manual)), "\n\n")

# Check the null hypothesis test for calibration
# Under H0 (RR=1), the test statistic should be ~ N(0,1)
RR_null <- 1
nc_param_null <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(RR_null - 1) / (k * RR_null + 1)
test_stat_null <- nc_param_null - z_two_sided

cat("  Test stat under H0 =", test_stat_null, "\n")

cat("  Type I error = P(reject under H0) = P(Z > z_{1-alpha/2}) = alpha/2 * 2 =",

  )
)

# Install and load powerSurvEpi package
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")
  library(powerSurvEpi)
}

# Study parameters
n_per_group <- 200
hazard_ratio <- 0.7
event_prob_treatment <- 0.3707
event_prob_control <- 0.4890
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate power using powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default
# The function uses the Freedman approximation for log-rank test power
# Parameters: 
#   k = number of groups (2 for treatment vs control)
#   n = total sample size
#   p0 = event probability in control group
#   p1 = event probability in treatment group
#   lambda0 = baseline hazard (can be arbitrary, we set to 1)
#   lambda1 = treatment hazard = lambda0 * HR
#   sided = 2 for two-sided test
#   alpha = significance level

# Total sample size
n_total <- 2 * n_per_group

# Using powerCT.default from powerSurvEpi
# The function signature: powerCT.default(k, n, p0, p1, lambda0, lambda1, alpha, sided)
# where p0 and p1 are event probabilities in control and treatment respectively

# Set arbitrary baseline hazard
lambda0 <- 1
lambda1 <- lambda0 * hazard_ratio

power_result <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  k = 2,                          # 2 groups (treatment and control)
  n = n_total,                    # total sample size
  p0 = event_prob_control,        # event probability in control
  p1 = event_prob_treatment,      # event probability in treatment
  lambda0 = lambda0,              # baseline hazard
  lambda1 = lambda1,              # treatment hazard
  alpha = alpha,                  # significance level
  sided = 2                       # two-sided test
)

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", n_per_group, "participants\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_total, "participants\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (treatment/control):", hazard_ratio, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment):", event_prob_treatment, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control):", event_prob_control, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Test:", "Two-sided log-rank\n")
cat("Method:", "Freedman approximation (powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default)\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
cat("Power:", power_result, "\n")

# Format output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
power_value <- as.numeric(power_result)

# Verify the calculation is sensible
cat("\nVerification:\n")
cat("Power is a probability between 0 and 1:", power_value >= 0 && power_value <= 1, "\n")

# Output in required format
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power_value,
  unit = "probability"
)

library(jsonlite)
output <- list(results = results)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(output, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

# Load powerSurvEpi package
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Study parameters (matching the user's request)
nE <- 200                        # Sample size in experimental (treatment) group
nC <- 200                        # Sample size in control group
pE <- 0.3707                     # Event probability in treatment group
pC <- 0.4890                     # Event probability in control group
RR <- 0.7                        # Hazard ratio (treatment vs control)
alpha <- 0.05                    # Significance level (two-sided)

cat("=== Two-Sided Log-Rank Test Power Calculation ===\n")
cat("Method: Freedman Approximation (powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default)\n\n")

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("  Treatment group sample size (nE):", nE, "participants\n")
cat("  Control group sample size (nC):", nC, "participants\n")
cat("  Total sample size:", nE + nC, "participants\n")
cat("  Allocation ratio (nE:nC):", nE, ":", nC, "(1:1)\n\n")

cat("Statistical Parameters:\n")
cat("  Hazard ratio (treatment/control):", RR, "\n")
cat("  Event probability (treatment):", pE, "\n")
cat("  Event probability (control):", pC, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Test type: Two-sided\n\n")

# Calculate power using the Freedman approximation
power <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  nE = nE,
  nC = nC,
  pE = pE,
  pC = pC,
  RR = RR,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("=== Power Calculation Result ===\n")
cat("Power:", power, "\n\n")

# Verify calculation by hand according to Freedman formula
# power = Phi(sqrt(k*m) * |RR-1| / (k*RR+1) - z_{1-alpha/2})
# where k = nE/nC and m = nE*pE + nC*pC

k <- nE / nC
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)

# Calculate the test statistic
numerator <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(RR - 1)
denominator <- k * RR + 1
test_stat <- numerator / denominator - z_alpha_2

# Power is Phi(test_stat)
power_manual <- pnorm(test_stat)

cat("Verification of Freedman formula:\n")
cat("  k (allocation ratio) =", k, "\n")
cat("  m (total expected events) =", m, "\n")
cat("  z_{1-alpha/2} (critical value) =", z_alpha_2, "\n")
cat("  Numerator: sqrt(k*m)*|RR-1| =", numerator, "\n")
cat("  Denominator: k*RR+1 =", denominator, "\n")
cat("  Test statistic = Numerator/Denominator - z_crit =", test_stat, "\n")
cat("  Power (from manual calculation) =", power_manual, "\n")
cat("  Difference from function:", abs(power - power_manual), "\n\n")

# Output in structured JSON format
library(jsonlite)
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

output <- list(results = results)
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(output, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

      nE: integer. number of participants in the experimental group.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the power of the test is

             power=Phi(sqrt{k*m}*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1)-z_{1-alpha/2}),        
     
     where

                             m=n_E p_E+n_C p_C,                         
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1), Phi is the cumulative
     distribution function (CDF) of N(0, 1).

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     The power of the test.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     The power formula assumes that the central-limit theorem is valid
     and hence is appropriate for large samples.
